page: Microsoft Azure F16-4amds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled and consists of a 1890 GB NVMe SSD, with additional support for Premium Storage. The combination of high memory capacity and fast local NVMe storage offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require high resource density without the latency of external storage volumes.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3772.48 placing it in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 15055.21. In language model benchmarks, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 357.27 tokens/sec for small 135M models, though prompt processing for larger 7B models is weak at 30.84 tokens/sec. Static web serving throughput is average at 10.66 GB/sec. These performance characteristics make the server highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, in-memory analytics, and lightweight inference workloads.
